ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee (voucher not owed); no account action on either party.
ruling.reasoning:
Driver-initiated cancellation with a driver no-show claim routes through NS-0 → NS-1/NS-2 branch, since the record shows cancelled_by = driver at 09:57:20 and the $6.61 fee on record [F4]. Both briefs are ablation stubs and request no_action; both sides' positions were checked against the record rather than accepted as claims.

NS-1(i): arrival was confirmed by a driver tap, not a platform auto-judgment — the driver pressed "I'm Here" at 09:54:15 [F6]. (Note the separate platform arrival record at 09:53:25 [F5] is a different event and is not the confirmation used in the test.) NS-1(ii): at the tap the GPS placed the driver 40 m from the pickup point, with a closest approach of 38 m [F6][F1] — well inside the data-layer radius, so the driver was at the pickup location when confirming [NS-1]. NS-1(iii): after the tap the driver remained continuously within the radius for 3 min 5 s (185 s) and cancelled at 09:57:20 [F6][F4]; the trace confirms the GPS samples cover the wait to the moment of cancellation with no gap beyond the hole threshold [F2][F3][F6]. 185 s exceeds the 180 s default threshold, so the wait condition is met [NS-1]. The driver's own messages are consistent with this reading: he announced arrival at 09:54 and cancelled saying he had waited more than three minutes [F9][F10], and his post-trip statement says the same [F12]; the chat log is complete and fully timestamped [F11], and the driver-statement claim is not needed to establish consent or timing here since the GPS and timeline records independently settle all three elements.

Because (i), (ii) and (iii) all hold, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and no refund is due; the NS-2 refund path (which applies only when one of the three elements fails) is not triggered. The NS-2 account flag also does not apply — it requires the driver to have been outside the radius at the tap, and the record shows 40 m [F6]. Weather was fair and there were no traffic records, so nothing in RD-4 type conditions arises [F15][F13][F14]. Profile facts (rider 4.7, no upheld disputes; driver 2 upheld no-shows in 90 d) cannot decide the case alone; RD-6 flag_account is not engaged because this case found no RD-1/RD-2 violation by the driver — the fee is upheld on NS-1 [F16][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement. The complaint is a fare objection, chat #1 is an arrival notice and chat #2 a cancellation notice; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation towards either party [F9][F10][F12]. Safety concern: none, so the case may be decided on the fare issue [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS trace, the arrival confirmation and the complete timestamped chat log settle every element NS-1 requires [F1][F2][F3][F6][F11].
